privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This explains what Nearby collects, why, and what we will never do with it. We have tried to write it in plain language rather than legal shorthand.

sections.heading: What we collect
paragraphs: Your email address, because it is how you sign in. We send a code to it each time, so there is no password to remember or to lose.
Anything you type in: your name, the reviews you write, and the details of any business you list.

Your approximate location, but only while the app is open and only if you allow it. We use it to sort places by how close they are. We do not track you in the background, and refusing simply means distances are measured from the city instead.
Which listings get opened, called or asked directions to. That is counted against the business rather than against you, so an owner sees how many people found them and never who.
A photo, if you choose one. Picking a profile picture or a photo of your business opens your gallery so you can hand us that file. We only ever receive the ones you pick.

A short code that identifies this installation of the app, along with the make of phone and the area you are in, rounded to about a kilometre. It is how we spot one person running a ring of accounts to post fake reviews, and it is used for nothing else. It is not an advertising identifier, it does not follow you into other apps, and clearing the app data resets it.

When something in the app fails, the message it failed with, which screen you were on, the app version and the kind of phone. It is how we find out that something is broken for real people rather than waiting to be told.

sections.heading: What we do not do
paragraphs: We do not sell your information to anyone.
We do not show adverts, so nothing about you is shared with advertisers.
We do not read your contacts, messages or files, and we never browse your photo library. Choosing a picture hands us that one file and nothing else.
We do not track where you are when the app is closed.

sections.heading: What other people can see
paragraphs: Reviews are public. Your name and the review appear on the listing, and the owner can reply in public.
If you list a business, everything on that listing is public: the name, address, hours, prices, photos and contact details you enter.
The places you save and the places you have looked at are private to you.
Your email address is never shown to anybody else, including the owner of a business you review.

sections.heading: When you report something
paragraphs: You can report a listing without an account, and then nothing at all about you goes with it.
If you are signed in, the report records that it came from you, so we can come back to you if we need to and so one account cannot flood the queue.
The business or the reviewer is never told who reported them.

sections.heading: Keeping it
paragraphs: We keep your information while your account exists. There is a Delete my account button in your profile settings, and it does what it says: your name, email, picture, reviews and any businesses you listed are removed, and none of it can be brought back.
If your account is removed any other way, reviews you wrote stay up but stop showing your name.
Error reports and the counts behind an owner dashboard are kept for ninety days and then deleted.

sections.heading: Where it is kept
paragraphs: Your information is held on servers run by our hosting provider, which may be outside your country. Access is limited to the people who keep Nearby running.

sections.heading: Children
paragraphs: Nearby is not intended for children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their information.

sections.heading: Asking us anything
paragraphs: You can ask for a copy of what we hold, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it. Get in touch and we will sort it out.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: The rules for using Nearby. Using the app means you agree to them.

sections.heading: Your account
paragraphs: You sign in with an email address, and we send a code to it. Keep that inbox to yourself, because anything done from your account is treated as done by you.
You can browse, search, read reviews and report a listing without an account. Saving a place, writing a review and listing a business all need one.
You must be at least 13 years old to use Nearby.

sections.heading: Reviews
paragraphs: Write about somewhere you actually went. Do not post reviews for a business you own or compete with, and do not accept anything in exchange for a review.
No abuse, no threats, no personal information about other people, and nothing untrue about a business.
We remove reviews that break these rules, and we may suspend an account that keeps doing it.

sections.heading: Listing a business
paragraphs: Only list a business you own or are authorised to manage. There is no way to take over somebody else's listing, on purpose.
We read every new listing before it goes live. Until then only you can see it, and you will get a notification either way, usually within a day. If we cannot publish it we will say why.
A published listing shows as unverified until we have confirmed it is yours. Verifying is our decision, and we may ask you for something that proves the connection.
Keep the details accurate. Wrong hours or a wrong price is the fastest way to lose the trust of the people the listing brings you.
Listing a business is free. Nothing on it is for sale, and paying us does not move you up the results.

sections.heading: When we take something down
paragraphs: We may hide a listing while we look into a report about it. While it is hidden, nobody but you can find it, and you will be told in the app.
We put it back if the report does not hold up.

sections.heading: Suspending an account
paragraphs: A suspended account cannot sign in, and everything it made leaves the directory: its listings, its reviews and the ratings those reviews contributed. Nothing is deleted, and lifting a suspension puts all of it back exactly as it was.
You will be told why. If you think it is a mistake, get in touch and we will look at it again.

Some suspensions are automatic. The app watches for the patterns that mean somebody is running several accounts to post fake reviews, and it acts when more than one of those patterns holds at once. A person reviews every automatic suspension that is questioned.

sections.heading: What we can and cannot promise
paragraphs: Listings come from business owners and reviews come from members of the public, so we cannot guarantee everything you read is accurate or current. Check with the business before relying on it.
Distances and opening hours are worked out from what a listing says and from where your phone reports it is. Treat both as a good guess rather than a guarantee.
We work to keep the app running, but we cannot promise it is available every minute.

sections.heading: Ending it
paragraphs: You can stop using Nearby whenever you like, and delete your account from your profile settings. That removes your reviews and any businesses you listed, and it cannot be undone.
We may suspend an account that breaks these rules or is used to harm somebody.

sections.heading: Changes
paragraphs: If these terms change in a way that affects you, we will say so in the app rather than quietly editing this page.
